sentences.text:
As against the compensation of Rs. 22,28,000/- claimed by the applicant/claimant by filing the claim application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 for injuries sustained in the motor accident on 24.04.2012 in a fatal accident along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of application till payment with costs.
3. The Tribunal, on a close scrutiny of the evidence led, held that the incident has taken place on 24.04.2012 in which the claimant received injuries due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle i.e. bus bearing registration no. CG 04 7147 which was driven by respondent no. 2 and respondent no. 3 is owner of the vehicle.

The claimant in his claim application has contended that on 24.04.2012 at about 9:45 pm near village Bangoli, Police Station Kharora, respondent no. 2 was driving the bus rashly and negligently has dashed against stationary tractor and due to which the bus got turtled, the claimant was sitting in the bus received grievous injuries.
One leg of the claimant has been amputated above the knee and another leg was amputated below the knee thereby he became permanent disabled.
The matter was reported to Police Station Kharora.
It was further contended by the claimant that at the time of accident he was the only earning member of the family.
At the time of accident, he was working as bus conductor thereby earning Rs. 7000/- per month, which would have been increased to Rs. 9000/- per month.

The claimant has claimed Rs.
22,28,000/- as total compensation towards different heads from respondent no. 2,3 and appellant jointly and severally.
In this case respondent no. 2 and 3 remained ex-parte before the tribunal and have also not filed their written statement.

Appellant has filed his written statement denying all the adverse allegation and has contended that respondent no. 2 and 3 have not produced vehicular documents like fitness, permit and license before the appellant, which is violation of the policy condition.

4. Being aggrieved by the impugned award dated 22.02.2019, the Insurance Company has preferred an appeal being MAC No. 1054/2019 seeking exoneration from liability, while the claimants have also preferred a cross-appeal under Order 41 Rule 22 of CPC seeking enhancement of compensation.
5. Smt. Swati Agrawal, learned counsel appearing for the appellant, submits that the offending vehicle was being used in violation of the insurance policy.
On the date of accident, the offending vehicle was not having any valid permit and fitness certificate.
She further submits that absence of valid permit and fitness certificate for a vehicle is a fundamental breach of policy condition.

In support of his contention, he placed his reliance upon an order passed in MAC No. 15 of 2016 (United India Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Bhola Rai and Others 2023 SCC Online Chh 2644 )
passed by Co-ordinate Bench of this Court on 21.07.2023.

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Bhola Rai and Others 2023 SCC Online Chh 2644 )
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record very carefully and minutely.

7. As regards the submission made by the learned counsel for respondents No. 1 & 2 that the offending vehicle was having a valid license and fitness certificate on the date of accident and there is no breach of policy.

The New India Insurance Company ... vs Dilip Rao on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90160963/
2 8.

entities.text: New India Insurance Company ... vs Dilip Rao
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the light of aforementioned facts, documentary evidence and oral evidence available on record,
it is evident that on the date of accident, the offending vehicle was not having valid fitness certificate issued by the competent authority.

9. In Pareed Pillai Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited reported in AIR 2019 Ker 9 (FB) , five Judges' Bench of Kerala High Court gave a ruling that the absence of fitness certificate for a Transport vehicle is a fundamental breach of policy conditions.

entities.text: Pareed Pillai Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited reported in AIR 2019 Ker 9 (FB)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Paragraph 17 is relevant for the purpose, is reproduced hereunder:

"17. Importance of the fitness/road worthiness of a vehicle, right from the time of registration of the vehicle, is further discernible from Rule 47 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 (referred to as Central Rules).
The said Rule deals with application registration of motor vehicles, which among other things, stipulates that it shall be accompanied by various documents.
Under sub-rule (1) (g), it is mandatory to produce road worthiness certificate in Form 22 from the manufacturers (Form 22A from the body builders).

On completing the formalities/procedures, 'Certificate Registration' is to be issued in terms of Rule 48 of the Central Rules in Form 23/23A,
as the case may be.

The said Rule contains a proviso, insisting that, when Certificate of Registration pertains to a transport vehicle, it shall be handed over to the registered owner only after recording the Certificate of Fitness in Form 38.

Validity of the Certificate of Fitness is only to the extent as envisaged under Rule 62 of the Central Rules, which mandates, as per the proviso that the renewal of a Fitness Certificate shall be made only after the Inspecting Officer or authorised Testing Station as referred to in sub-section 1 of Section 56 of the Act has carried out the test specified in the table given therein."

10. In view of aforementioned facts and circumstances of the case in the light of ruling by the High Court of Kerala in the matter of Pareed Pillai (supra), it is held that the insurance company has proved the breach of policy conditions by the owner and driver.

Apart from this, the learned Claims Tribunal has also recorded a finding that the deceased was not equally responsible for cause of accident, therefore, the question that there was contributory negligence on the part of claimant does not arise.
The said finding is correct finding of fact based on evidence on record.

11. The issue with regard to first pay the amount of compensation and thereafter to recover the same from the owner of offending vehicle has also been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Shamanna Vs. Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., reported in (2018) 9 SCC 650 in which Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that in case of breach of policy conditions, pay and recover can be ordered.

entities.text: Shamanna Vs. Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Company Ltd., reported in (2018) 9 SCC 650
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. In view of above, I direct the appellant/insurance company to first deposit entire amount of compensation along with interest before the Claims Tribunal and thereafter, to recover the amount so deposited by it from respondent no. 6 and 9, driver and owner of the offending vehicle in accordance with law.

sentences.text: Also, interest awarded by the tribunal @ 7.5% is on the higher side.

Thus, the insurance company is directed to pay the amount of compensation along with interest @
6% per annum.
14. As a result, the appeal of the appellant/Insurance Company is allowed in part.
